audit_findings.title: Historical OE may contain the disposed aerospace business
audit_findings.mechanism: Aerospace earnings, D&A, capital expenditures and working-capital cash flows may enter the historical OE series and therefore the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash flows from the historical aerospace reportable segment are presented within each cash flow statement category in the consolidated statements of cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that consolidated cash-flow categories include discontinued aerospace cash flows, while the valuation uses seven pre-sale observations and declares no perimeter adjustment. Whether the OE ledger separately removed those amounts remains unresolved. The possible error is material: aerospace generated filed 2023 discontinued earnings of $223 million, D&A of $81 million and capex of $106 million, versus the $861.6 million anchor, and the business was sold for $5.6 billion. Contamination across multiple trend years could therefore change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct each 2016–2022 and 2024 OE observation from continuing operations, explicitly removing aerospace earnings, D&A, capex and working-capital movements, then recompute the trend anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The post-year-end Benepack acquisition is absent from the perimeter ruling
audit_findings.magnitude: $218 million total consideration; $19 million acquisition-date NCI; $11 million H1 2026 operating earnings; computed $0.80 per share for the full consideration
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition creates post-2025 operating earnings, financing costs and a 20% noncontrolling claim that are absent from the anchor but partly present in current cash, debt and equity balances.
audit_findings.evidence: In January 2026, the company acquired an 80 percent capital share of Benepack’s European beverage can manufacturing business from ORG Technology Co. Ltd. (ORG), for total consideration of $ 218 million (or € 184 million), subject to customary closing adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its filed scale is insufficient to change the conclusion. Benepack produced $11 million of operating earnings in the first half of 2026, only 1.3% of the $861.6 million anchor. Even treating the entire $218 million transaction consideration as omitted common-equity value produces only about $0.80 per share, versus the $8.55 gap between the $54.12 bull value and the $62.67 market price. The $19 million NCI is only 0.15% of base equity value. Direction is mixed because omitted earnings understate value, while omitted financing costs and the 20% outside claim overstate it.
audit_findings.action: Add a Benepack pro-forma OE schedule using filed operating results, interest, taxes and maintenance reinvestment; attribute only 80% to Ball or deduct NCI, and confirm that acquisition cash and assumed debt are treated consistently.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method earnings may lack corresponding reinvestment deductions
audit_findings.magnitude: $27 million of 2025 affiliate earnings; 3.1% of the $861.6 million anchor; computed $1.64 per share bull-case dollar-for-dollar sensitivity
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate accounting earnings may enter OE although investee maintenance capex, debt service and working-capital requirements are outside Ball's consolidated reinvestment deductions.
audit_findings.evidence: Equity investments in which the company exercises significant influence but does not control are accounted for using the equity method of accounting.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the $27 million was retained or replaced with distributable cash is unresolved. Nevertheless, removing the entire filed amount from the anchor dollar-for-dollar would reduce the bull valuation by about $1.64 per share before considering that the trend method would dilute a one-year adjustment. That is well below the $8.55 gap between bull value and market price, so the demonstrated earnings-line scale does not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $27 million through the OE ledger and obtain affiliate distributions, maintenance capex, debt service and required contributions; rerun only with Ball's proportionate distributable owner earnings.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 OE observation may retain disposal and insurance gains
audit_findings.magnitude: $81 million filed Saudi Arabia gain within $41 million net business-consolidation income; computed maximum dollar-for-dollar bull sensitivity of $4.92 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Unremoved non-operating gains could raise the 2025 OE observation and the fitted trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, the company recorded income of $ 41 million, primarily composed of the $ 81 million gain on the sale of the Saudi Arabia business, and insurance proceeds for replacement costs related to the 2023 fire at the company’s Verona, Virginia, extruded aluminum slug manufacturing facility, partially offset by costs for previously announced facility closures and the loss related to the aluminum cups business transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the gains but not their treatment in the OE ledger. Even the conservative assumption that the full $81 million sale gain increased the anchor dollar-for-dollar would add about $4.92 per share to bull value, still less than the $8.55 gap to the market price; its actual effect should be smaller because it affects only one of nine trend observations and is partly offset within the filed $41 million net line. The insurance component is not separately quantified. Closure and restructuring cash costs should not be automatically added back.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2025 OE adjustment ledger, remove the disposal and replacement-insurance gains, retain recurring cash closure and restructuring costs, recompute the trend anchor and document the resulting sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved tariff exposure is outside normalized OE
audit_findings.mechanism: A retrospective tariff liability could require a cash payment outside the bridge, while unrecovered prospective duties could reduce normalized OE and growth margins.
audit_findings.evidence: While the outcome of this matter is uncertain at this time, the company believes it is reasonably possible any such additional tariffs, interest and penalties could be owed and impact the company’s results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is no longer purely forward-looking: the 2026 10-Q reports expenses associated with tariff contingencies, but combines them with facility-closure costs and says recovery is being pursued. The company still provides no separable charge, challenged import base or estimable total loss. The record therefore demonstrates current exposure but cannot establish its valuation magnitude, recurrence or customer pass-through, leaving materiality unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the tariff assessment periods and import base, isolate the tariff portion of 2026 charges, identify amounts reserved or paid, assess recovery probability and customer pass-through, and rerun separate one-time bridge and recurring-OE cases.

audit_findings.title: Pension cash funding may exceed the expense retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $176 million underfunded liability at June 30, 2026, or $0.64 per share; $29 million expected 2026 funding versus $12 million expected pension cost
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash funding above pension expense would reduce OE, or the unfunded obligation could be deducted once in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Contributions to the company’s defined benefit pension plans are expected to be approximately $ 29 million in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential mismatch exists, but its scale is modest. The $176 million underfunded liability equals about 1.4% of the $12.596 billion base equity value and $0.64 per share. Expected 2026 funding exceeds expected pension cost by $17 million, only 2.0% of the $861.6 million anchor. Either treatment would leave every scenario below the market price. Deducting both the deficit and normalized excess funding would double count the same claim.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension expense to normalized cash funding and choose either an incremental OE deduction or a one-time funded-status bridge deduction; rerun once and document avoidance of double counting.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.0 million in FY2020, equal to 4.5% of filed D&A and 3.5% of the $861.6 million anchor; computed $1.54 per share base dollar-for-dollar sensitivity
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A left as an expense would depress one historical OE observation and potentially the fitted anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $30.0m (4.5% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative and cannot overstate value. Even treating the full $30 million as a recurring dollar-for-dollar anchor increase would add only about $1.54 per share to base value, far below the $16.53 gap between base value and market price. Because the amount affects only the 2020 observation in a nine-point trend, the actual valuation effect would be smaller.
audit_findings.action: Classify the $30 million residual from filed depreciation schedules and rerun only for components demonstrated to be eligible non-economic add-backs.
